- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.4) over recent days, model tends to overcorrect upward — reduce forecast peak by 5–10% relative to prior high.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 80), model often overshoots in next 5–7 days — cap forecast at +5% above prior peak or align with 30-day moving average.
- If sentiment turns positive after a downtrend (e.g., +0.3+), model often overreacts — dampen forecast rise by 3–5% in first 3 days.
- Model consistently underestimates true price in early 30-day window when sentiment is neutral or mildly negative — add 2–4% to forecast for first 5 days.
- When sentiment is volatile (alternating +/– 0.3), model tends to overfit short-term noise — smooth forecast by averaging last 5–7 days’ values before projecting.
- If true outcome is below 70 and sentiment is negative, model often ignores downward momentum — reduce forecast by 3–6% for next 3–5 days.
- Model frequently overestimates 30-day mean in high-sentiment environments — adjust downward by 1–3% if sentiment > 0.2 for 3+ consecutive days.
